records.title: use closure table for version chain
records.body:
Our current approach to linking versions of objects in DataONE and Metacat is to provide a pointer in the SystemMetadata for each object that points at the objects that it `obsoletes` and those that are `obsoletedBy` it.  This represents a doubly-linked list that can be traversed to reconstruct version information.  The `obsoletes` and `obsoletedBy` fields are in the Metacat postgres database as columns in the system_metadata table, with the abbreviated structure:

```guid, obsoletes, obsoleted_by```

From a hierarchical data modeling perspective, this structure is called an adjacency list, and allows one to trace the version chain through a series of queries, each of which walks the version chain either forwards or backwards. Without support for hierarchical queries (which are proprietary and perform poorly), this generally means issuing `n-1` queries, where `n` is the length of the version chain.

Much has been written about querying hierarchical data. Some good background reading is:

- https://www.slideshare.net/billkarwin/models-for-hierarchical-data
- https://dirtsimple.org/2010/11/simplest-way-to-do-tree-based-queries.html

From the first set of slides, and other reading, I have concluded that closure tables are a much more efficient and fast way to store and query this hierarchical data.  It involves creating a new table for just the hierarchical information, and creating one row for each link in the version chain, including links at each level of the hierarchy.  This table structure allows a single query to retrieve all parent and child information in the tree, and so is extremely fast, and only marginally more expensive in terms of storage.  The articles linked above explain much more thoroughly than I will here, but the essences is that the closure table contains the following columns:

```parent, child, depth```

A simple query to get all of the versions for a given object would be:

```sql
select * from closure_table where parent = 'P1';
```

We'll need to develop out a more mature design, and an API to go along with this, but I think closure tables will allow us to provide efficient version information in our services with a new API.  Below I attach my notes on the design and use of closure tables for reference.

[closure-tables-notes.pdf](https://github.com/NCEAS/metacat/files/4234178/closure-tables-notes.pdf)

Comments and expansion of ideas appreciated.  @csjx, @amoeba, @gothub, @taojing2002 @laurenwalker

records.title: Normalize Vitest scratch roots and prove abnormal-exit cleanup
records.body:
## Plain-English Summary

The stable Vitest runner creates scratch roots without a complete Windows custody or cleanup contract. On Windows it sets `TMPDIR`, but Node selects `TEMP` and then `TMP`, so child processes can escape the intended root. The runner also does not remove its own `pcvt-*` root.

## Current State — 2026-09-01

- Current `dev` has no `scripts/clean-stale-test-temp.mjs` cleaner. The old broad-sweeper proposal exists only in preserved, never-landed work and must not be treated as current code.
- `scripts/run-vitest-stable.mjs` creates a new `pcvt-*` root and a `PAPERCLIP_HOME` for each invocation.
- It sets only `TMPDIR` and does not perform owned-root cleanup.
- The 2026-09-01 S: allocation later released without a scratch cleanup, so exact causation is still unknown. Do not attribute that incident to retained `pcvt-*` roots without file-level evidence.
- The correct direction is producer ownership plus #20's external identity-bound process owner, not a broad prefix/age sweeper.

## Why It Matters

Killed, timed-out, or failed runs can leave large trees, locked files, and secret-shaped test residue. A broad sweeper can also delete an unrelated or still-active directory that merely has a matching name. The cleanup must therefore prove exact ownership and child quiescence before deletion.

## Fix / Action Status

1. Allocate one `eph-paperclip-vitest-<UTC>-<rand6>` outer root per stable-runner execution.
2. Put every invocation root and `PAPERCLIP_HOME` below that outer root.
3. Set `TEMP`, `TMP`, and `TMPDIR` to the same owned root.
4. Write an owner-only manifest before child launch and a privacy-safe terminal receipt.
5. Refactor direct `process.exit(...)` paths so normal failure still reaches bounded cleanup.
6. Require child-tree quiescence before bounded recursive removal; retry only known transient lock errors and verify absence.
7. Use #20's reviewed identity-bound owner for timeout or abnormal-exit cleanup. In-process exit hooks are best-effort only.
8. Keep unknown, legacy, secret-bearing, or nonconforming roots report-only until ownership is proven. Do not add a broad age/prefix deleter.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Windows children use the same owned `TEMP`, `TMP`, and `TMPDIR` root.
- [ ] Normal success and normal failure remove only the current exact owned root and verify absence.
- [ ] Timeout and killed-run proof uses the external identity-bound owner and leaves zero owned process members.
- [ ] Receipts report duration, exit status, logical bytes, child count, cleanup result, residual paths, free-space samples, and caller tag without secrets or private raw paths.
- [ ] Negative proof covers Windows temp escape, injected `EBUSY`, a real locked file, killed-mid-run custody, secret-shaped residue, and a legacy nonconforming root.
- [ ] A deliberately broken ownership manifest fails for the exact reason before restoration.
- [ ] Focused tests, real hook, hosted CI, and independent review pass.

## Not A Blocker / Blocks

This is not a required code change for the current #47/#63/#80/#84/#87/#88 delivery if the real hook runs inside #20's reviewed identity-bound runner with a disk admission and cancellation floor. It remains a serious disk-stability and repeatability follow-up.

## Related Docs / Evidence Links

- Windows hook/process ownership: #20
- Shared task-owned Job runner: iMelki/agent-settings#685
- Node temporary directory selection: https://nodejs.org/api/os.html#ostmpdir
- Node process exit semantics: https://nodejs.org/api/process.html#event-exit
- Node bounded recursive removal: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html#fsrmpath-options-callback
- Workspace disk incident context: iMelki/agent-settings#285

records.title: 3️⃣ DFS/BFS
records.body:
# 꼭 필요한 자료구조 기초
- 탐색 Search : 많은 양의 데이터 중 원하는 데이터를 찾는 과정
    - 프로그래밍에서는 그래프, 트리 등 자료구조 안에서 탐색하는 문제를 자주 다룸.
    - 대표적인 탐색 알고리즘이 DFS, BFS
    - DFS와 BFS를 이해하려면 자료구조인 스택과 큐에 대한 이해가 필요.

- 자료구조 Data Structure : 데이터를 표현하고 관리, 처리하기 위한 구조
    - 스택과 큐는 자료구조 기초개념으로 두 핵심적인 함수로 구성됨
        - 삽입(Push) : 데이터를 삽입
        - 삭제(Pop) : 데이터를 삭제
        - 오버플로우(Overflow)와 언더플로우(Underflow)도 고민해야함.
            
            오버플로우는 특정한 자료구조가 수용할 수 있는 데이터 크기가 가득 찬 상태에서 삽입연산을 수행할 때 발생
            언더플로우는 자료구조에 데이터가 전혀 들어가있지 않은 상태에서 삭제 연산을 수행할 때 발생
            

## 스택 Stack

선입후출, 후입선출 First In Last Out, Last In First Out

```python
# 스택예제 5-1

stack.append(5)
stack.append(2)
stack.pop()
stack.append(1)
stack.pop()

print(stack) # 최하단 원소부터 출력
print(stack[::-1]) # 최상단 원소부터 출력 
```

파이썬에서 스택을 이용할 때 별도 라이브러리 필요없이 append()와 pop() 메서드를 이용하면 스택자료구조와 동일하게 동작. append()는 리스트 가장 뒤쪽에 데이터를 삽입하고 pop()메서드는 리스트 가장 뒤쪽에 데이터를 꺼냄

## 큐  Queue

선입선출 First In First Out

```python
# 큐 예제 5-2

from collections import deque

queue = deque()

queue.append(3)
queue.append(6)
queue.popleft()
queue.append(2)
queue.popleft()

print(queue) # 먼저 들어온 순서대로 출력
queue.reverse() # 다음 출력을  위해 역순으로 바꾸기
print(queue) # 나중에 들어온 원소부터 출력
```

파이썬으로 큐를 구현할 때는 collections 모듈에서 제공하는 deque 자료구조를 이용. deque는 스택과 큐의 장점을 모두 채택한 것으로 데이터를 넣고 빼는 속도가 리스트 자료형에 비해 효율적이며 queue 라이브러리 이용보다 간단. 또한 대부분의 코딩테스트에서  collections 모듈과 같은 기본 라이브러리 사용을 허용.

deque 객체를 리스트 자료형으로 바꾸려면 list() 메서드를 이용. list(queue) 

## 재귀함수 Recursive Function

자기자신을 다시 호출하는 함수 

```python
def recursive_function() :
	print("재귀함수를 호출합니다")
	recursive_function()

recursive_function()
```

위의 경우 재귀함수를 무한히 호출하기  때문에 아래와 같은 오류메시지가 출력될 것.

```python
RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded while pickling an object
```

재귀의 최대 깊이를 초과. 파이썬 인터프리터의 호출 횟수 제한을 벗어났기 때문. 

재귀함수는 프랙탈 Fractal 구조와 흡사. (시에르핀스키의 삼각형 SSierpinski Triangle) 

### 재귀함수의 종료조건

재귀함수 사용시 언제 끝날지 종료조건을 명시해야 한다.

```python
def recursion_function(i) :
	# 100번째 출력할 때 종료되도록 조건 명시
	if i == 100:
		return 
	print(i, "번째 재귀함수에서", i+1, "번째 재귀함수를 호출")
	recursive_function(i+1)
	print(i, "번째 재귀함수를 종료합니다.")

recursive_function(1)
```

컴퓨터 내부에서 재귀함수 수행은 스택 자료구조 이용. 계속 호출했을 때 가장 마지막에 호출한 함수가 먼저 수행을 끝낸야 그 앞의 함수 호출이 종료되기 때문에. 따라서 스택 자료구조를 활용하는 상당수 알고리즘은 재귀함수를 이용해 간편히 구현할 수 있다. DFS 가 그 대표적인 예. 

그  외에도 팩토리얼 Factorial 문제가 있다.

```python
# 팩토리얼을 반복적으로 구현
def factorial_iterative(n) {
	result = 1
	# 1부터 n까지 곱하기 
	for i in range(1, n+1) :
		result *- i
	return result
}

# 팩토리얼을 재귀적으로 구현
def factorial_recursive(n) {
	if n <= 1 : # n이 1 이하인 경우 1을 반환
		return 1
	# n! = n * (n-1)!을 코드로 작성
	return n == n * factorial_recursive(n-1)
}

# 각각 방식으로 구현한 결과 출력
print("반복으로 구현" , factorial_iterative(5))
print("재귀적으로 구현", factorial_recursive(5))
```

실행결과는 동일하지만 반복문 대신  재귀함수를 사용할 경우 재귀함수의 코드가 더 간결. 간결해진 이유는 수학의 점화식(재귀식)을 그대로 옮겼기 때문. 수학에서 점화식은 특정한 함수를 자신보다 더 작은 변수에 대한 함수와의 관계로 표현한 것을 의미한다.

records.title: [Initiative #329][EPIC #331][Phase #340] Build the implication graph and SCCs in Rust
records.body:
Task: 1

Implement Phase 1 by creating a new self-contained `cdg` module that derives
Zsigmondy-forced residue classes and computes strongly connected components of
the resulting implication graph.

Step 1 - Module setup:
- Create the file `rust-engine/src/cdg.rs`.
- Register the module in `rust-engine/src/main.rs` as `mod cdg;`, placed
alphabetically before `mod distributed;` in the third module block. Use plain
`mod` (not `pub mod`).

Step 2 - Derive forced residue classes and candidate mapping:
- Add a helper that enumerates divisors `d > 1` of `2e+1` for a component, where
`2e+1 = two_e + 1` (since `PrimePower.two_e` already stores `2*e`). Use the `for
d in 1..n { if n % d == 0 }` trial-loop idiom.
- For each divisor `d`, treat `d` as the modulus of the forced residue class `q
≡ 1 (mod d)`.
- Build a prime-to-component-index map from the `components: &[PrimePower]`
slice, for example `HashMap<u64, Vec<usize>>` keyed by `.p`, using the
`entry(...).or_insert_with(Vec::new).push(i)` idiom (modeled on the
`prime_counts` grouping in `math_utils.rs::composite_tonelli_shanks`). This map
replaces any ad-hoc `.iter().rposition(...)` lookups.
- For each component `i` and each divisor `d > 1` of its `two_e + 1`, collect
candidate component indices `j` whose prime satisfies `components[j].p % d ==
1`. Implement this as a simple generic `p % d == 1` check. Do not reuse the
fixed-modulus `IsValidMod8`, `Mod3`, `Mod5`, or `Mod9` helpers.
- Expose the per-component forced-candidate sets as `Vec<Vec<usize>>` indexed by
component index.

Step 3 - Build the directed graph and Tarjan SCC:
- Build a directed adjacency-list graph `Vec<Vec<usize>>` over component
indices, where an edge `i -> j` means "choosing component `i` forces a candidate
`j` for some divisor `d`". Derive these edges from the forced-candidate sets
from Step 2.
- Implement an iterative Tarjan SCC algorithm over the adjacency list as a
net-new implementation, using an explicit work stack instead of recursion
(consistent with the explicit-stack pattern in `dfs_tree.rs`). Do not add an
external crate for this.
- Expose the SCC results as a `component_index -> scc_id` array (`Vec<usize>`
sized to `num_components`) and per-SCC member lists (`Vec<Vec<usize>>`). Use the
same positional index scheme as `SearchBackbone` and `active_mask`.
- Provide a single public constructor, for example `Cdg::new(components:
&[PrimePower]) -> Cdg`, that runs the derivation from Step 2 and the graph/SCC
computation together, returning the forced-candidate sets, the adjacency list,
and the SCC lookup.
- Add `#[cfg(test)]` unit tests with small concrete component sets that verify
divisor enumeration, candidate mapping, and SCC grouping, modeled on the inline
test style in `obstruction.rs`.
===============================================================================

Task: 2

Implement Phase 2 by extending `SearchBackbone` with implication metadata and
populating it during backbone construction, without changing existing pruning
behavior.

Step 1 - Extend the `SearchBackbone` struct in `rust-engine/src/backbone.rs`:
- Add fields for the forced-candidate sets per component and the SCC lookup (the
`component_index -> scc_id` array and per-SCC member lists) produced by
`cdg.rs`.
- Keep the existing `compatibility_matrix`, `min_n_product`, and
`num_components` fields unchanged. Add the new fields alongside them, not in
place of them.
- Use owned types (`Vec<...>`) for the new fields so they clone cleanly, since
`SearchBackbone` and related state are cloned and snapshot/restored during DFS.

Step 2 - Populate the new fields inside `SearchBackbone::new`:
- Reuse the existing O(n²) loop (lines 41–67) that compares every component pair
`(i, j)`. Inside the loop, determine implication edges using the resolved
`sigma_factors` and prime data already in scope (`comp_i`, `comp_j`,
`pre_resolved_factors[i]`, `pre_resolved_factors[j]`).
- Precompute the divisor list of `two_e + 1` once per component `i`, outside the
inner `j` loop, to avoid recomputation. Inside the inner loop, test
`components[j].p % d == 1` for each divisor `d > 1`.
- Assemble the per-component forced-candidate sets from these pairwise results.
- After the loop completes, build the adjacency list and run Tarjan SCC by
calling the `cdg` module constructor (or its lower-level functions). Store the
resulting SCC lookup on the struct.
- Do not modify how `compatibility_matrix` or `min_n_product` are computed or
written. The existing bit-setting and product logic must produce identical
results.

records.title: [MEDIUM][数据库查询] buildIssueContext() N+1：循环内逐条查祖先 issue
records.body:
## 问题

`packages/server/src/routes/sessions.ts:100-158`

```typescript
while (currentId && chain.length < MAX_ANCESTOR_DEPTH) {
  if (visited.has(currentId)) break
  visited.add(currentId)
  const [issue] = await db.select().from(issues).where(eq(issues.id, currentId))
  if (!issue) break
  chain.push(issue)
  currentId = issue.parentId
}
```

最多 10 次 DB 查询获取祖先链。

## 影响

每次创建 session 关联 issue 时触发，issue 层级深时延迟明显。

## 建议修复

使用递归 CTE 一次查询获取整条链：

```sql
WITH RECURSIVE ancestors AS (
  SELECT * FROM issues WHERE id = $1
  UNION ALL
  SELECT i.* FROM issues i JOIN ancestors a ON i.id = a.parent_id
)
SELECT * FROM ancestors LIMIT 10
```

need to fix n+1 prob when querying messages. its much to slow. 

Something like 

  WITH RECURSIVE subtree AS (
      -- Base case: direct children of the requested parent
      SELECT m.*, 1 AS depth
      FROM messages m
      WHERE m.parent_id = $1

      SELECT m.*, s.depth + 1
      FROM messages m
      JOIN subtree s ON m.parent_id = s.message_id

records.title: [P2] If maintaining the driver fork, replace the bespoke recursive PID tree and boot self-test
records.body:
The kernel process-to-image mapping uses a custom unbalanced binary search tree with recursive insertion, lookup/maintenance paths, and a maximum-sized image-name array in every node. Driver creation also runs a custom tree algorithm self-test.

The mapping and whitelist evaluation cache support real enforcement needs, but the bespoke tree implementation and maximum-sized per-node storage are not intrinsically required. An unbalanced tree also has insertion-order-dependent depth, which deserves scrutiny in kernel code.

Evidence:
- [PROCESSIDTREE and recursive operations](https://github.com/mikeev261/HidHide/blob/e1263ae848e4409fbe645bdbd003580eb86af7a9/HidHide/src/Config.c#L17)
- [Runtime consistency test](https://github.com/mikeev261/HidHide/blob/e1263ae848e4409fbe645bdbd003580eb86af7a9/HidHide/src/Config.c#L394)
- [Driver startup self-test call](https://github.com/mikeev261/HidHide/blob/e1263ae848e4409fbe645bdbd003580eb86af7a9/HidHide/src/Logic.c#L30)

Scope:
This is conditional on continued maintenance of a custom driver fork. If the product remains only a companion to the existing signed driver, isolate/archive the fork instead of investing in a kernel rewrite.

Proposed direction:
- Evaluate an appropriate supported kernel table implementation with bounded/balanced lookup behavior.
- Allocate image-name storage to actual required length.
- Move algorithm verification into tests and remove the production boot self-test once replacement behavior is adequately covered.
- Preserve process-exit cleanup, PID reuse handling, synchronization, whitelist invalidation, and IRQL/allocation constraints.

Acceptance:
- Document the driver-maintenance decision before implementation.
- If implemented, validate process churn, adverse insertion order, allocation failure, cleanup, and cache invalidation.
- Run appropriate driver verification in a test environment.

records.title: [REFACTOR] Taxonomy Model Normalization
records.body:
## 🎯 Feature Description

Restructure the entire taxonomic data model to create a unified, normalized taxonomy system by:
1. Renaming `Taxon` to `Species` for clarity
2. Creating new `Taxa` model as central taxonomic entity
3. Implementing recursive synonym relationships within Taxa model
4. Simplifying Plant-Taxa relationships

## 🤔 Motivation & Problem Analysis

**Current Structural Issues:**
- **Fragmented Taxonomy**: Taxonomic information split between `Taxon`, `Infraspecific`, and relationship tables
- **Complex Relationships**: Plant taxonomy built through multiple junction tables (`RelPlantSynonym`)
- **Inconsistent Hierarchy**: No unified way to represent taxonomic relationships
- **Maintenance Challenges**: Difficult to manage synonyms and taxonomic updates

**Proposed Solution Benefits:**
- **Unified Model**: Single `Taxa` model handles all taxonomic ranks
- **Simplified Relationships**: Direct Plant-Taxa relationship with proper hierarchy
- **Better Performance**: Reduced JOIN complexity in taxonomic queries
- **Enhanced Features**: Support for complex taxonomic relationships and history

## 📊 Implementation Plan

### New Model Structure
```python
class Taxa(BaseModel):
    RANK_CHOICES = [
        ('family', 'Family'),
        ('genus', 'Genus'), 
        ('species', 'Species'),
        ('subspecies', 'Subspecies'),
        ('variety', 'Variety'),
        ('form', 'Form'),
        ('cultivar', 'Cultivar'),
    ]
    
    # Taxonomic identity
    name = models.CharField(max_length=255)
    rank = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=RANK_CHOICES)
    author = models.JSONField(blank=True, null=True)  # Will use new author structure
    
    # Taxonomic hierarchy
    parent = models.ForeignKey('self', on_delete=models.CASCADE, null=True, blank=True, related_name='children')
    accepted_taxon = models.ForeignKey('self', on_delete=models.CASCADE, null=True, blank=True, related_name='synonyms')
    
    # Taxonomic status
    is_accepted = models.BooleanField(default=True)
    taxonomic_status = models.CharField(max_length=50, default='accepted')
    
    # Additional fields
    custom = models.JSONField(blank=True, null=True)
    
    class Meta:
        constraints = [
            models.UniqueConstraint(
                fields=['name', 'rank', 'parent'], 
                name='unique_taxonomic_entity'
            )
        ]

# Simplified Plant model
class Plant(BaseModel):
    accepted_taxa = models.ForeignKey(Taxa, on_delete=models.RESTRICT, related_name='plants')
    # Remove: infraspecific, synonyms, synonyms_infra fields
    # All taxonomic info now through Taxa model
```

### Synonym Relationship Simplification
```python
# Current complex structure (to be removed)
class RelPlantSynonym(BaseModel):
    plant = models.ForeignKey(Plant, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    synonym_taxon = models.ForeignKey(Taxon, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    synonym_infraspecific = models.ForeignKey(Infraspecific, on_delete=models.CASCADE, null=True)

# New simplified structure within Taxa model
# Synonyms are recursive relationships within Taxa
```

## 📊 Impact Assessment

- **Severity/Impact**: [High]
- **Effort**: [High]
- **Breaking Changes**: [Yes]
- **Migration Strategy**: Comprehensive data migration with validation tools

## ✅ Implementation Checklist

### Phase 1: Model Restructuring
- [ ] Create new Taxa model with recursive relationships
- [ ] Rename Taxon to Species (optional - can be handled by Taxa.rank)
- [ ] Update Plant model to use Taxa instead of Taxon/Infraspecific
- [ ] Remove RelPlantSynonym model

### Phase 2: Data Migration
- [ ] Create migration script to convert Taxon -> Taxa
- [ ] Create migration script to convert Infraspecific -> Taxa
- [ ] Migrate synonym relationships to Taxa recursive relationships
- [ ] Validate taxonomic hierarchy integrity

### Phase 3: API & Business Logic
- [ ] Update all model managers and queries
- [ ] Update API serializers and views
- [ ] Update admin interface for new taxonomy
- [ ] Create taxonomic validation utilities

### Phase 4: Advanced Features
- [ ] Implement taxonomic tree navigation
- [ ] Add taxonomic history tracking
- [ ] Create taxonomy import/export utilities
- [ ] Develop taxonomic reconciliation tools
